title: Jonah and the Witness
premise: Lena Underhill, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, is hired by an anxious stranger to prove that a murder will not happen — a murder the client describes in unsettling detail, dated four days hence, inside the cathedral's sealed crypt. Following a donor ledger disguised as a medieval mortuary roll, Lena and her reluctant ally, Detective Sergeant Ivo Marsh, discover the crypt holds the body of a whistle-blowing accountant and a conspiracy reaching the cathedral chapter itself. The intended victim is the client, Jonah Reyes, who staged his own predicted death to force someone to look. In the climax beneath the crypt's locked door, Lena chooses love over duty — saving Jonah and exposing Dean Wycliffe's corruption at the cost of her own sanctuary, ending with her walking out of the cathedral that defined her, finally belonging to herself.
about_author: Gideon Blackwood is the pen name of a former cathedral conservator who spent a decade restoring illuminated manuscripts before turning to crime fiction. They write in the margins of old buildings, convinced that every archive keeps at least one secret worth killing for.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A nervous man named Jonah Reyes pays triple her fee to prove a murder will not occur — his own — on Friday, in the crypt. Lena, who has quietly solved three 'accidents' the police ignored, recognizes the pattern of staged deaths in his details. Emotional beat: wary fascination; the archivist's instinct that this record is already written.

chapters.title: The Mortuary Roll
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Searching the archive for the crypt's access history, she finds a donor ledger disguised as a medieval mortuary roll — names of the living recorded among the dead. Three of those names match her old 'accidents.' Emotional beat: cold dread as her private obsession becomes a living case.

chapters.title: The Reluctant Sergeant
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. DS Ivo Marsh, humiliated when Lena's past deductions proved right, refuses to hear her out — until she shows him the ledger and the crypt's maintenance log, altered last month. Emotional beat: pride giving way to uneasy partnership; two lonely people circling the same truth.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Keeps
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The crypt's inner chamber has been opened and resealed — recently. Inside, behind the tomb of the cathedral's founder, they find a hidden cavity built to hold a body, and fresh mortar. Someone prepared a grave in advance. Emotional beat: the sacred made sinister.

chapters.title: The Dean's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The mortuary roll's cipher decodes to modern donations: Dean Wycliffe has been laundering money through restoration funds, and the 'accidents' were whistle-blowers. The next name on the roll, in fresh ink, is Jonah Reyes. Emotional beat: Ivo's faith in the institution cracking alongside the case.

chapters.title: Confession at Compline
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah reveals he is the accountant who found the ledger, that he tipped off Wycliffe's fixer by accident, and that predicting his own murder was the only way to buy protection. Lena realizes she isn't his investigator — she's his alibi and his shield. Emotional beat: guilt, tenderness, the beginning of love against duty.

chapters.title: The Locked Door
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Friday arrives. The crypt is sealed for a private 'conservation inspection' authorized by the chapter; Ivo is suspended on fabricated charges. Lena hides inside as the fixer and an accomplice arrive to make the prophecy true. Emotional beat: terror transposed into stillness — the archivist as witness.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Living
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Locked out of the investigation, Ivo uses the decoded ledger to trace the fixer's payments to a shell company — and finds Wycliffe's signature buried in a decade of transactions. He races back to the cathedral as the service bells begin. Emotional beat: redemption through stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Witness Below
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the crypt, Lena steps out of the dark and names what she has read aloud, buying minutes with words while the fixer closes in. Jonah is nearly pushed into the prepared grave; Lena takes the blow meant for him. Ivo arrives with police as Wycliffe descends to finish it himself. Emotional beat: the climax — love and duty fused into one act of witness.

chapters.title: Ex Libris
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, weeks later. Wycliffe is charged; the cathedral chapter dissolved; the true mortuary roll entered as evidence. Offered her job back, Lena declines, taking the archive's most dangerous volume with her as a loan. She and Jonah walk out through the west doors into ordinary light. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won belonging — to a person, and to herself.
